verdict.rationale: `ultrametric init --dry-run` previews the changes before anything is written. A hands-on probe confirmed it lists every file it would create (SKILL.md under both .agents/skills and .claude/skills) without writing. The skills then land as ordinary local project files that docs say can be committed and shared, so they can be read in full after install. missing for 10: evidence that the dry run shows file contents rather than just paths, documentation of exactly what instructions or scripts each skill file contains, a hands-on read of the installed files after a real install. [2026-10-14 re-judge parity audit (owner-product lane): full 7 -> partial 5, the audit standard: the recorded dry run previews file names only and the preview's content (file list vs full instruction text) is undocumented — weaker evidence than skills-cli's keyless --list enumerating every skill's full trigger description, which sits at partial 5. The owner product does not get a higher reading of thinner recorded evidence. Ultrametric-affiliation governance, README §9.]
